definitions.gloss: gyuhi; sweetened soft mochi; Turkish-delight-like rice cake
definitions.explanation: A soft, pliable type of mochi made by kneading glutinous rice flour with sugar and starch syrup. Used extensively in traditional Japanese confections.

examples.japanese: {求肥|ぎゅうひ}で{餡|あん}を{包|つつ}む。
examples.english: To wrap bean paste in gyuhi.

examples.japanese: この{和菓子|わがし}は{求肥|ぎゅうひ}のもちもちした{食感|しょっかん}が{特徴|とくちょう}だ。
examples.english: This Japanese sweet is characterized by the chewy texture of its gyuhi.

examples.japanese: {求肥|ぎゅうひ}は{普通|ふつう}の{餅|もち}と{違|ちが}って{時間|じかん}が{経|た}っても{硬|かた}くなりにくい。
examples.english: Unlike regular mochi, gyuhi doesn't harden easily even over time.

notes:
A type of soft, elastic mochi used as a key ingredient in many traditional Japanese confections ({和菓子|わがし}). Made from {白玉粉|しらたまこ} (glutinous rice flour) or {餅粉|もちこ} kneaded with sugar and {水飴|みずあめ} (starch syrup).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {求肥|ぎゅうひ}{餅|もち}: gyuhi mochi
- {求肥|ぎゅうひ}で{包|つつ}む: to wrap in gyuhi
- {求肥|ぎゅうひ}を{作|つく}る: to make gyuhi

USED IN:
- {大福|だいふく}: daifuku — mochi stuffed with sweet filling
- {雪見|ゆきみ}だいふく: yukimi daifuku — ice cream wrapped in gyuhi
- {練|ね}り{切|き}り: nerikiri — molded Japanese confections

ETYMOLOGY:
Originally written as {牛皮|ぎゅうひ} (cow skin) because the soft, stretchy texture was likened to cow hide. The characters were later changed to {求肥|ぎゅうひ} to avoid the unappetizing association.
